history_policy: This version hash-inherits every V10 workload, mode, jobs, checksum, timing boundary, engine-availability, acceptance, synchronization, and runtime-dispatch decision. It versions the opt-in allocation and exact per-cycle GC-pause inventory and removes only those implemented metrics from the pending inventory; any later workload, boundary, jobs, checksum, metric, or acceptance change creates another version.
change: Adds exact successful Context backing allocation/growth/release operations and bytes, logical GC-cell fresh/reused/relocation/delegated allocation and free counts with issued size-class storage bytes, and the raw nanosecond duration of every completed minor/full collection. The two allocation domains remain separate, pause sample overflow rejects the artifact, and scored timing rows remain uninstrumented.

tier_attribution.scope: one fresh zig-js process and context per workload and structural variant; Context backing attribution begins after the profiler storage itself is allocated and before arena/Context construction
tier_attribution.invocation: one inherited full-work call with the frozen jobs and lane-zero input
tier_attribution.equivalence: For warmup and invocation independently, each base/variant pair must select the same non-empty set of tree-walker, VM, baseline, optimizer, optimizer-OSR, and deoptimization paths and allocate exactly the same number of environments. Exact tier, runtime, synchronization, allocation, GC-pause, and worker counters remain visible rather than normalized away; every Wasm workload must record an invocation-phase Wasm dispatch.
tier_attribution.timing_isolation: Attribution uses fresh opt-in processes and contexts outside every scored timing row; normal contexts retain the original allocator chain, disabled contention counters, null execution-attribution pointer, and no GC-pause sample storage.

recognizer_audit.prohibited: Every representative workload identifier is absent from engine source. Identifiers exist only in the owned workload, manifest, and benchmark tooling.
